html:
The Abbey of Saint Gall was a Benedictine monastery founded in 719 at the place where the Irish monk Gallus had lived as a hermit, in what is now eastern Switzerland.

Under the Carolingians it became one of the great centres of learning north of the Alps. Its monks copied books, wrote music and kept a school. The Plan of Saint Gall, drawn about 820, is the oldest surviving plan of a whole monastery. The library still holds one of the oldest collections of manuscripts in the world.

The town of St. Gallen grew around the abbey, later a centre of linen and embroidery. The abbey was closed in 1805, after the Helvetic Republic. Its precinct is a UNESCO site, and part of the long story of Christianity in the Alps begun by Irish missionaries and spread by the Carolingians.
sum: The Abbey of Saint Gall was a Benedictine monastery founded in 719 at the place where the Irish monk Gallus had lived as a hermit, in what is now eastern Switzerland.
